study: GR00T N1.5 stage timing on NVIDIA's FULL-PIPELINE TensorRT path — compiled counterpart of speed/stage_time_eager.py
stages_note: transform = policy.apply_transforms (on already-decoded frames); backbone = eagle_tensorrt_forward (ViT + LLM engines + pixel-shuffle/mlp1/embedding-merge torch glue); head = action_head_tensorrt_forward (vlln + state engines, then per step: action_encoder + DiT + action_decoder engines + torch glue); other = everything else in get_action (obs copy, prepare_input/collate, unapply/denormalize). *_total = summed over the denoise steps. Mean of two engine builds.

host_and_glue.note: host + glue = e2e - engine time; on this path it grows with steps (Euler loop + 3 engine handoffs per step)

instrumentation_overhead.note: per-stage cuda-synced timers add ~0.3-0.5 ms; the stage split is read from the instrumented pass, the latency law from the uninstrumented one

cross_validation_result: Stage fit (instrumented): fixed 7.54 ms + 1.575 ms/step vs the uninstrumented sweep law 7.38 + 1.523 ms/step (the instrumented pass is expected to sit slightly higher: per-stage syncs).

tenancy.note: one idle co-resident GPU process (8.7 GB allocated, 0% SM) throughout; the desktop X server briefly at 8% SM in one build-B block; host load average 4.6-8.3 from other work. Per-block logs are in the raw files.

noise_floor.estimator: mean of 25 synced reps per grid point per build (median e2e also kept); two builds averaged

metric_span: Per-stage cuda-synced wall time within policy.get_action() on the full-TensorRT path, every grid step count; each engine's in-pipeline time summed per inference.
input_provenance: a recorded (simulated) GR1 observation, not synthetic data: NVIDIA demo_data/robot_sim.PickNPlace ds[0] (same step as the sweep latency and as the eager stage timing).
